claims.text: Resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion in high-entropy alloys is governed by formation of a stable, passivating surface oxide layer.
A stable, passivating oxide layer acts as a barrier to mechanical wear.
A stable, passivating oxide layer acts as a barrier to corrosion.
The proposed initial material is a high-entropy alloy containing equal or near-equal proportions of multiple principal elements.
Exposure to a harsh corrosive mechanical environment promotes or tests formation of the stable passivating oxide layer.
The relevant harsh environment comprises high temperature, high humidity, and mechanical stress.
Formation of the protective oxide layer prevents wear.
Formation of the protective oxide layer prevents corrosion.
An alloy possessing the stable passivating oxide layer will have improved resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion relative to a matched alloy lacking that layer.
The prediction should hold for high-entropy alloys with stable, passivating oxide layers.
The prediction may fail for alloys with unstable or non-passivating oxide layers.
Oxide-layer composition and structure may affect the validity of the hypothesis.
Specific environmental conditions may affect the validity of the hypothesis.
